answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks via latency multilateration. Anchor nodes measure round-trip times to map an agent onto a network atlas, isolating collocated clones along a coordinate ridge. Each agent must verify its location against an oasis of reference beacons. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of provisioning geographically dispersed network interfaces per identity. However, asymmetric routing paths introduce latency jitter that can falsely reject honest participants.
